deep.reconstruction:
This page has no formulas. It is the title and introductory paragraph of the fair-copy manuscript of Riemann's paper 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines flüssigen gleichartigen Ellipsoids'. The paper was published in Abh. Kgl. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9 (1861) and is reprinted in his Gesammelte Werke.

Content of the page:
(i) Dirichlet's last work, edited posthumously by Dedekind, opened a new route for studying the motion of a homogeneous fluid ellipsoid whose elements attract under Newtonian gravity. That work is 'Untersuchungen über ein Problem der Hydrodynamik', Abh. Göttingen 8 (1860).
(ii) The problem is mathematically attractive in itself, quite apart from its origin in the question of the figures of celestial bodies.
(iii) Dirichlet carried the solution through completely only in the simplest cases.
(iv) Programme: rewrite the equations of motion in a form independent of the chosen initial instant. One way is to find the laws governing the change of the semi-axes a, b, c and of the motion of the fluid relative to the principal axes.
(v) Dirichlet's memoir is presupposed, but Riemann warns that its notation could not be kept unchanged.

Modern restatement of the programme (my gloss, anticipating the next page): Dirichlet's ansatz is that positions are linear in initial positions, x = F(t) x0. Riemann factors F with respect to principal axes, roughly F = R1(t)^T diag(a,b,c) R2(t), after rescaling x0 by diag(1/a0,1/b0,1/c0). Here R1 gives the orientation of the ellipsoid's axes and R2 encodes the internal motion relative to those axes. He then seeks an autonomous ODE system for a, b, c and the two angular-velocity vectors. This is the framework that yields the Riemann ellipsoids (S-type and related), Riemann's stability criteria, and the Dedekind reciprocity between figure rotation and internal vorticity.
